objective: By the end of this lesson you can say exactly when 14 CFR 91.175 requires a missed approach, find the missed approach point on any approach, and fly the published or ATC missed approach by reference to instruments, including early missed approaches, circling missed approaches and holding at the missed approach fix.
why: The missed approach comes at the busiest, lowest and often darkest moment of an IFR flight. Pilots who decide late, turn early or get lost in the avionics hit terrain; pilots who have briefed it and fly it by rote simply climb away and try again.

prereading.what: Missed approach: reasons to go missed, balked landings, early climbs, how the MAP is depicted, and steeper than standard climb gradients.
prereading.label: IPH 4-39 to 4-41

prereading.what: Missed approach: climb gradient, early missed approaches, circling missed approaches, radar vectors, alternate missed approaches and balked landings.
prereading.label: AIM 5-4-21, pp 5-4-58 to 5-4-61

prereading.what: Pilot and controller roles on a missed approach: when to go missed, what to tell ATC, and what to request.
prereading.label: AIM 5-5-5, pp 5-5-3 to 5-5-4

prereading.what: Missed approach technique, the 91.175 minimums and the pilot's judgment of flight visibility.
prereading.label: IFH 10-21 to 10-22

prereading.what: How the MAP is found on each type of approach and how missed approach instructions are written on the chart.
prereading.label: IFH 1-21 to 1-23

prereading.what: Go-arounds: power, attitude and configuration, ground effect and common errors.
prereading.label: AFH 9-11 to 9-12

prereading.what: Automation management: levels of automation and the anticipate, act, verify habit.
prereading.label: RMH 7-1 to 7-3

warmup: You reach the DA on an ILS and you can see the approach lights, but nothing else. Do you land, keep descending, or go missed? What would change your answer?

key_terms.def: Where you must start the missed approach if you can't continue: the DA on an approach with vertical guidance, or a fix, NAVAID or time from the FAF on a nonprecision approach.
The MSL altitude on a precision or vertically guided approach where you decide to continue or go missed.
The lowest MSL altitude on a nonprecision or circling approach until you have the required visual references.
The part of the approach from the MAP to a fix where an initial or en route segment begins.
Climb required for each nautical mile flown, in feet per NM. The standard missed approach gradient is 200 ft/NM.
A missed approach ATC gives you instead of the published one, or one put in effect by NOTAM.
A go-around started past the MAP or below the MDA or DA, where the published missed may not protect you.
The GPS waypoint that is the MAP on an RNAV approach. It is always a fly-over waypoint.
Finishing the missed approach climb while flying the holding pattern, when the procedure says so.
The display that shows which autopilot modes are engaged and which are only armed.

body.p: A missed approach is what you fly when you can't land from an instrument approach. 14 CFR 91.175 tells you when it is required, not just allowed.
**Going below DA or MDA.** You may not descend below the MDA, or continue below the DA/DH, unless all three of these are true [[60:471|14 CFR 91.175(c)]]:

bullets: You are always in a position to descend to a landing on the intended runway at a normal rate, using normal maneuvers [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(1)]].
Flight visibility is at least the visibility on the approach chart [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(2)]].

At least one listed visual reference for the runway is distinctly visible and identifiable: approach lights, threshold, threshold markings or lights, REIL, visual glideslope indicator, touchdown zone or its markings or lights, runway or runway markings, or runway lights [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)]].

callout.text: Approach lights alone take you only to 100 ft above the touchdown zone elevation. To go lower on the lights, you must also see the red terminating bars or the red side row bars [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)(i)]].

body.p: **When you must go missed.** You must *immediately* fly a missed approach when those requirements are not met while below the MDA, or on arrival at the MAP (including a DA), or at any time after that until touchdown [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(e)(1)]]. While circling at or above the MDA, you must also go missed if you can't distinctly see an identifiable part of the airport, unless you lost it only because of a normal bank [[60:473|14 CFR 91.175(e)(2)]].

head: What you find
What you do
rows: At the DA or MAP, not enough visual reference to land
Runway in sight, but flight visibility is below the chart minimum
Missed approach. Only you can judge flight visibility, whatever the report says [[23:313|IFH 10-22]]
Below the MDA or DA, visibility lost or runway environment no longer visible
You decide a safe approach or landing isn't possible, or ATC tells you to go missed
People, equipment or animals on the runway, or the approach becomes unstabilized

callout.text: On an LPV or LNAV/VNAV approach you go missed when you reach the DA without the required references. Don't wait for the GPS distance to count down to zero [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d7]].

check.q: At the DA you see only the approach lights. How low may you go on them alone?
check.a: To 100 ft above the touchdown zone elevation, unless you also see the red terminating bars or red side row bars. You also need the chart flight visibility and a normal descent position [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)]].

body.p: The MAP is where the final approach ends and the missed approach segment begins [[29:190|IPH 4-50]]. How you find it depends on the approach you fly [[33:450|AIM 5-4-20f5]].

head: Approach
How you find the MAP
rows: Reaching the DA/DH on the glideslope or glidepath [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]
VOR or NDB with the station on the airport
Nonprecision, aid away from the airport, no MAP fix
A course and DME, a cross radial from a VOR, or an RNAV (GPS) waypoint [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]
The MAWP, always a fly-over waypoint [[33:99|AIM 1-1-17b5(h)(3)]]

body.p: On every chart, the MAP for the lowest minimums is where the solid course line ends and the dotted missed approach line begins, in both the plan and profile views [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]. Straight-in nonprecision and circling procedures share the same MAP [[33:450|AIM 5-4-20f5]].

**Timing.** A table on the chart gives the distance from the FAF to the MAP and the time it takes at groundspeeds in 30-knot steps. Work out your groundspeed from approach speed, TAS and the wind on final, then start a clock at the FAF [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]. Burbank example: 5.4 NM from FAF to MAP takes 3:36 at 90 knots and 2:42 at 120 knots [[29:186|IPH Figure 4-25]].

callout.text: On an approach that uses timing, start a clock or stopwatch at the FAF. The time from the FAF is how you find the MAP on that approach [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

check.q: On the Burbank LOC your groundspeed on final is 120 knots. What time do you fly from the FAF to the MAP?

body.p: A clearance for an instrument approach includes a clearance to fly the published missed approach, unless ATC tells you something else [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]].
The full missed approach text is in the pilot briefing at the top of the chart. The icons in the profile view show only the first steps, four at most [[33:419|AIM 5-4-5m7(c)]]. Always read the text.

head: Form
Example
rows: Straight ahead, then a turn to the hold
"Climb to 900, then climbing right turn to 2,500 direct ABC VOR and hold" [[23:42|IFH 1-23]]

body.p: The missed approach course starts at the MAP and goes to a fix where you enter holding. ATC normally gives you further instructions before you get there. The fix is often an IAF, so you can try another approach without flying from the hold to an IAF [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

Daggett RNAV (GPS) RWY 26 example: climb to 8,000 direct AMAKE, then on track 270° to BINTE, then on track 192° to NULMN and hold, continuing the climb in the hold to 8,000 [[29:187|IPH Figure 4-26]].

callout.text: Brief the published missed before every approach, even when the tower will probably give you other instructions [[29:182|IPH 4-42]]. The missed comes when workload is highest, so study and master it before you start the approach [[23:312|IFH 10-21]].

check.q: Your approach clearance says nothing about a missed approach. What are you cleared to fly if you miss?
check.a: The published missed approach procedure, unless ATC instructs otherwise [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]].

body.p: Obstacle protection on the missed approach assumes you start it at the DA/DH, or at the MAP and not lower than the MDA [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].
It also assumes you climb at least 200 ft per NM, unless the chart notes publish a higher gradient. A higher gradient ends at a stated altitude or fix [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

The gradient is in feet per NM, but your VSI shows feet per minute. The TPP booklets have tables (page D1) that convert gradient to climb rate for your groundspeed, and a faster groundspeed, such as a tailwind on the climb-out, needs a higher climb rate [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. You can also work it out: groundspeed ÷ 60 is the NM you cover each minute, and each NM needs the gradient's feet, so climb rate (fpm) = gradient (ft/NM) × groundspeed ÷ 60. Check it against the TPP table: 297 ft/NM at 180 knots is 892 fpm, and 297 × 180 ÷ 60 = 891 [[29:34|IPH Figure 1-17]].

**If you can't make the gradient.** At Burbank, if you can't meet 334 ft/NM, use the separately published LOC Y RWY 8, whose higher minimums need only 200 ft/NM [[29:186|IPH Figure 4-25]]. Newer charts may publish two lines of minimums: a lower one that needs the steeper climb and a higher one that doesn't [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]. At Daggett, the LPV DA# of 2,217 ft needs 220 ft/NM to 8,000; the other LPV DA is 2,438 ft [[29:187|IPH Figure 4-26]].

callout.text: Preplan it. You must know before the approach that your airplane can meet the missed approach climb gradient [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. If you can't, use the other minimums, ask for another approach, or tell ATC (ACS IR.VI.C.S6). Also tell ATC any time you can't climb at least 500 fpm [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

body.p: Speed matters for turns too. Approach category minimums protect the missed approach climb surface and turn at that category's speeds [[29:148|IPH 4-8]]. If you fly faster than the top of your category's speed range, use the minimums of the higher category that fits that speed. A Category B airplane circling at 145 knots uses Category D minimums [[29:148|IPH 4-8]].

check.q: The chart requires 250 ft/NM and you expect 100 knots groundspeed on the missed. What climb rate do you need?

body.p: You can start a missed approach early. Reasons include a GPS integrity (RAIM) alert, an ATC instruction, or deciding that a safe approach or landing isn't possible [[33:98|AIM 1-1-17b5(g)]] [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].

The protected airspace has buffers for normal maneuvers, but **no allowance for an early turn**. So, unless ATC clears you otherwise, fly the approach as charted to the MAP, at or above the MDA or DA/DH, before you turn [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]] [[23:312|IFH 10-21]].

bullets: **Lateral:** keep flying the final approach course to the MAP [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].

**Vertical:** climb to the missed approach altitude, unless a maximum altitude is charted between the FAF and the MAP. Then obey the maximum, even if that means continuing to descend on final [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].
**GPS:** activating the missed before the MAWP switches the CDI to ±1 NM, but the receiver keeps navigating to the MAWP. Don't turn before the MAWP [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].

body.p: Orlando Executive ILS or LOC RWY 7: the missed approach is a climb to 1,200 *maximum* to SOTCO, to keep you below the airspace for Orlando International. If you go missed before BUVAY, you may need to keep descending to 1,200 before flying on to the MAP [[29:181|IPH 4-41]] [[29:184|IPH Figure 4-23]].

callout.text: RAIM alert before the FAWP: don't descend. Fly to the MAWP via the FAWP, fly the missed and contact ATC. RAIM alert after the FAWP: start a climb and fly the missed approach [[33:98|AIM 1-1-17b5(g)]].

check.q: Two miles before the MAP on a VOR approach, ATC tells you to go missed and gives no other instructions. The published missed starts with a climbing left turn. When do you turn?
check.a: At the MAP. Fly the approach course to the MAP at or above the MDA, then turn [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]] [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].

chunks.title: Circling missed approaches and balked landings

body.p: If you lose visual reference while circling, fly the missed approach for the approach you flew, unless ATC gives you an alternate [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21c]].

**Turn toward the runway first.** Make an initial climbing turn toward the landing runway, and keep turning until you are established on the missed approach course [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21c]]. You may be circling either way, so the path you fly to join the course depends on where you are when you lose sight [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21c]].

callout.text: Turning away from the runway toward the missed approach course can take you outside the protected areas. The climbing turn toward the runway is what keeps you inside the circling and missed approach obstruction clearance areas [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21c]].

body.p: **Balked landing.** If you go around past the MAP, from below the MDA or DA, or from a circling approach, the published missed does not necessarily give obstacle clearance or separation from traffic [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]]. Contact ATC as soon as possible for an amended clearance. If you can't, try to rejoin a published segment of the missed and follow its route and altitudes. If that no longer makes sense, consider staying visual and landing, or a circle-climb over the airport [[33:452|AIM 5-4-21h]] [[33:453|AIM 5-4-21h]].
Think about this before every approach: the expected weather, your airplane's performance, charted obstacles, the departure procedure for that runway, and other traffic [[33:453|AIM 5-4-21h]].

callout.text: At an airport without an operating tower you may not be able to talk to ATC down low. Fly the missed without delay and call ATC when you can [[33:453|AIM 5-4-21h]].

check.q: Circling to land in left traffic, you lose sight of the airport on the downwind leg. Which way do you turn?
check.a: A climbing left turn, toward the landing runway, continued until you are established on the missed approach course [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21c]].

chunks.title: ATC: reports, vectors and alternate missed approaches

body.p: **Tell ATC.** Advise ATC that you are going missed, and say why unless ATC started it [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]]. Then ask for what you want next: another approach, holding for better weather, or your alternate [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21f]].

callout.text: Phraseology example: "Marathon 564, missed approach, request clearance to Chicago." [[29:105|IPH 2-45]]

body.p: **Radar vectors.** Where radar service is provided, follow vectors ATC gives in place of the published missed [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21d]]. Controllers may vector a radar-identified airplane on a missed approach when it helps the pilot or the controller [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5b]].

**Alternate missed approach.** ATC may issue one, for example when the primary missed approach NAVAID fails during the approach [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]]. Some airports have a preplanned one. Its text is not on the chart, but its holding pattern may be shown. When a NOTAM puts it in effect, it is a mandatory part of the procedure [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]].

head: ATC issues the alternate missed
Your options
rows: After you have begun the approach
You may reject it if it needs equipment the published approach doesn't [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]]
Accept the whole procedure, ask for a different approach, or coordinate other action such as going to your alternate [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]]

callout.text: Can't comply? Say so right away. Report when you can't climb at least 500 fpm [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]], and tell ATC if you can't meet a holding speed restriction [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)(2)]].

body.p: Before leaving the published missed for anything else, make sure you have climbed to a safe altitude, especially without radar. Leaving it early may not give terrain clearance [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21g]].

check.q: Tower says: "Go around, fly runway heading, climb and maintain 3,000." The published missed is a right turn to a VOR. What do you fly?
check.a: The tower's instructions. ATC can specify other missed approach instructions, and you comply with those instead of the published missed [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21d]].

chunks.title: GPS, autopilot and moving maps on the missed

body.p: **Non-WAAS GPS.** The receiver needs you to sequence it past the MAWP onto the missed. Know how your receiver does it, and do it after the MAWP. If you don't, it shows an extension of the final course and the distance from the MAWP keeps growing [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].

bullets: If the first missed approach leg is a course rather than direct to a waypoint, you must take extra steps to set the course [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].
WAAS receivers sequence past the MAWP on their own when the missed was designed for RNAV. You can select the missed early, but navigation still goes to the MAWP first [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d7]].
On WAAS, CDI scaling changes suddenly to missed approach scaling at about the departure end of the runway, or when you select missed approach guidance [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d5]].

body.p: **Autopilot.** The AFM or its supplement gives the procedures and limits for using the autopilot on an approach, including the lowest altitude you may keep it engaged [[29:176|IPH 4-36]]. Set the missed approach altitude in the altitude preselector once you are established: after glideslope capture on a precision approach, or once level at the MDA on a nonprecision one. If you leave the MDA in the window, the flight director can't guide you correctly on the missed [[29:176|IPH 4-36]] [[29:177|IPH 4-37]].

**Watch the mode annunciators.** Use anticipate, act, verify: know what should happen, push the button, then check that the airplane does it [[30:51|RMH 7-2]]. A change of navigation source can drop the autopilot to a lower mode, such as wings level [[30:52|RMH 7-3]].

callout.text: Automation surprised you on the missed? Fly the airplane. Reduce the level of automation, fly by hand, and take time to fix it once you are climbing on course [[30:51|RMH 7-2]].

body.p: **Moving map.** An MFD moving map shows where you are relative to NAVAIDs, waypoints, airspace and terrain [[23:29|IFH 1-10]]. Glance at it to confirm you are turning the right way toward the right fix, and cross-check it with your CDI.

check.q: Past the MAWP, your non-WAAS GPS shows the distance increasing and no missed approach leg. What happened?
check.a: The missed approach wasn't activated. The receiver won't sequence past the MAWP until you do it [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].

chunks.title: Fly it step by step: the missed approach climb

body.p: A go-around is three things, in this order: power, attitude, configuration [[24:182|AFH 9-11]]. The IFH missed approach sequence matches: set climb pitch while setting climb power, configure for climb, turn to the right heading, advise ATC and request further clearance [[23:312|IFH 10-21]].

bullets: 1. **Decide and say it:** "Going missed." Delay is what makes a go-around dangerous [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].
2. **Power:** full or maximum allowable power, smoothly and without hesitation. Carburetor heat off, if installed [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].
3. **Attitude:** set the climb pitch on the attitude indicator. Power makes the nose rise and yaw left, so hold forward pressure and right rudder, then rough trim [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].
4. **Flaps:** once the descent has stopped, raise them in small steps as the manufacturer recommends, letting the airplane accelerate [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].
5. **Positive rate of climb:** gear up, if retractable, after the flaps are at least partly up [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].
6. **Navigate:** fly the published or ATC missed. Turn only at or after the MAP [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].
7. **Talk:** "missed approach," the reason, and your request [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].
8. **Checklist:** when climbing and stable, run the POH go-around or climb items. Airplane control comes first in this high-workload phase [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

head: ACS standard
Tolerance
rows: Promptly, and report it to ATC (ACS IR.VI.C.S1)
Positive rate of climb, accelerate to the appropriate airspeed ±10 knots (ACS IR.VI.C.S3)

callout.text: The IPH crew briefing uses callouts like "go-around thrust, flaps 15, positive climb, gear up" [[29:182|IPH 4-42]]. Flying alone, say your own version out loud. SRM covers task allocation and automation management even for a single pilot [[30:56|RMH 8-3]]. With a crew, SOPs may have the monitoring pilot call "I have control, going around" if two challenges get no response [[59:26|AC 120-71B 6.6.2.3]].

check.q: You add full power and the nose pitches up hard. What do you do?
check.a: Hold the climb attitude with forward elevator pressure and right rudder, then rough trim. Letting the nose rise too early can cause a stall at low altitude [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

chunks.title: Holding at the missed approach fix, then what?

body.p: When the missed approach ends in holding, fly the track and pattern shown on the plan view. The text names the NAVAID or radials that define the fix [[23:42|IFH 1-23]].

head: Entry
Arriving from
How
rows: Fly to the fix and turn to follow the pattern [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]]
At the fix, turn outbound to a heading 30° into the holding side for 1 minute, then turn to intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]]
At the fix, parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding side for 1 minute, turn more than 180° toward the holding side, and return to the fix or intercept inbound [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]]

bullets: Maximum holding speed: 200 KIAS from the MHA to 6,000 ft MSL, 230 KIAS from 6,001 to 14,000 ft [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].
Inbound leg: 1 minute at or below 14,000 ft MSL [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]].
Report the time and altitude when you reach the holding fix, and report when you leave it [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].
You may need more climb in the hold before going back to the IAF or on to the alternate [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21g]].

body.p: **Pick your next move.** After a missed approach, ask for a specific action: another approach, holding for improved conditions, or your alternate [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]]. ATC clears you to the alternate, a holding fix or back into the approach sequence as traffic allows [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5b]].

head: Option
Ask yourself
rows: Did I miss because of something I can fix, like my setup? Is the weather still at or above minimums?
Is improvement coming soon? How long can I hold and still reach my alternate with a reserve?
Your IFR fuel plan covered the destination, the alternate, then 45 minutes at normal cruise [[60:468|14 CFR 91.167(a)]] [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. Every extra approach or hold eats into that.

check.q: You reach the missed approach holding fix at 4,000 ft. What do you report to ATC?
check.a: The time and altitude on reaching the holding fix [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

chunks.title: Risk: deviations, decisions, configuration and automation

body.p: **Deviations from the procedure or ATC (R1).** The published missed protects you only on the missed approach segment, from or above the MAP, with a climb of 200 ft/NM or more [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]]. An early turn [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]] or leaving the procedure before reaching a safe altitude [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21g]] throws that protection away. Question any instruction you don't understand before you fly it.

**Holding, diverting or trying again (R2).** Each choice uses fuel and adds workload. Decide on the ground what you will do after a missed. A single pilot who prepares for a diversion, with frequencies and approaches ready, can act with crew-like efficiency [[30:57|RMH 8-4]].

**Configuration (R3).** Big speed and configuration changes late in an approach hurt situational awareness and make the decision at the DA or MAP harder [[29:177|IPH 4-37]]. A high-drag go-around, where the pilot forgets to raise flaps or gear, can drain the airplane's energy near the ground [[24:103|AFH 4-17]]. Raising all the flaps at once can make the airplane settle [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].
**What leads to an early missed, or a go-around below DA or MDA (R4):**

bullets: GPS RAIM alert, or the receiver doesn't switch to approach mode [[33:98|AIM 1-1-17b5(g)]].
An unstabilized approach. In IMC, go around if not stabilized by 1,000 ft above the airport elevation [[24:177|AFH 9-6]].
Shallow fog that hides the runway at the flare [[29:179|IPH 4-39]].
Losing the runway environment after descending below the DA or MDA [[29:180|IPH 4-40]].
People, equipment or animals on the runway [[29:180|IPH 4-40]].
An ATC instruction [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].

callout.text: Two things delay go-arounds: landing expectancy, the belief that this approach is sure to end in a landing, and pride, the belief that going around admits failure [[24:182|AFH 9-11]]. Brief yourself before the FAF: "Not in sight at the DA, I go."

body.p: **Automation (R5).** Unexpected reprogramming triggers errors, and pilots who always rely on the autopilot can lose manual skill [[30:51|RMH 7-2]]. One of the most common errors is not moving to a lower level of automation when things change [[30:51|RMH 7-2]]. Be ready to fly the missed by hand.

check.q: Name the two attitudes the AFH says delay a go-around.

body.p: From the AFH go-around list [[24:183|AFH 9-12]], plus missed approach errors from the AIM and IPH:

bullets: Not recognizing that the approach should be abandoned, indecision, or delay [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].
Late or abrupt power, or not using maximum allowable power [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].
Wrong pitch attitude, or not correcting for torque and P-factor [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].
Not configuring the airplane, or trying to climb out of ground effect too soon [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].
Turning toward the missed approach course before the MAP [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].
Turning away from the runway when the circling approach is lost [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21c]].
Forgetting to sequence the GPS past the MAWP [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].
Leaving the MDA set in the altitude preselector [[29:177|IPH 4-37]].
Not telling ATC about the missed, or not asking for the next clearance [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].
Loss of aircraft control [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].

check.q: Why is climbing out of ground effect too soon a problem in a low go-around?
check.a: Ground effect lowers induced drag, so the performance is borrowed. Climb too soon and the airplane may not climb or even hold altitude at full power [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].

On the right, an airplane decides to miss near the runway end and makes a dashed climbing turn toward and over the runways.

f3.alt: Approach chart for ILS or LOC RWY 7 at Orlando Executive, marked not for navigation. Highlighted note: a descent to 1,200 may be required when executing an early missed approach. Missed approach: climb to 1,200 maximum altitude via I-ORL east course to SOTCO, then climbing left turn to 1,500 via ORL R-049 to OVIDO and hold. Profile shows BUVAY at 3 DME, a 1,200 restriction and a FAF to MAP table of 5.5 NM with times from 5:30 at 60 knots to 1:50 at 180 knots.

f4.caption: Figure 4-25. Missed approach point depiction and steeper than standard climb gradient requirements.
f4.alt: Burbank ILS or LOC Z RWY 8 chart over the LOC Y RWY 8 chart. A highlighted note says missed approach obstructions require a minimum climb gradient of 334 ft/NM; if unable, see LOC Y Rwy 8, whose higher minimums meet the standard 200 ft/NM. The profile shows the MAP where the solid course line turns into the dotted missed approach line, and a FAF to MAP table of 5.4 NM: 5:24 at 60 knots, 3:36 at 90, 2:42 at 120, 2:10 at 150, 1:48 at 180.

f5.alt: Daggett RNAV (GPS) RWY 26 chart. Notes say the missed approach requires a minimum climb of 220 ft per NM to 8,000. The minimums box shows two LPV lines: LPV DA# 2217-1 and LPV DA 2438-1 3/4, plus LNAV and circling minimums. Missed approach: climb to 8,000 direct AMAKE, on track 270 to BINTE, on track 192 to NULMN and hold, continue climb-in-hold to 8,000.

f7.alt: A standard right-turn holding pattern at a fix inside a circle split by a line 70 degrees from the holding course. The shaded sector (a) is the parallel entry, sector (b) the teardrop entry, and the two (c) sectors the direct entry, with dashed lines showing the parallel and teardrop paths. No wind.

scenario.title: Night LOC approach, fog and a busy missed
scenario.setup: You are single pilot at night, flying a LOC approach with the autopilot coupled. The weather is reported at minimums with patchy fog. The chart notes say the missed approach requires 300 ft/NM to 1,800 ft. You expect about 100 knots groundspeed on the climb-out. You have 1 hour 40 minutes of fuel, and your alternate, with good weather, is 30 minutes away.

questions.q: Before the FAF: what climb rate does the 300 ft/NM note mean for you, and what if your airplane can't do it?
questions.a: 100 knots is 1.67 NM a minute, so about 500 fpm. You must preplan that you can meet the gradient [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. If you can't, use minimums that don't need it, ask for another approach, or tell ATC before you start [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

questions.q: Past the MAP you see the runway lights and descend below the MDA. At about 300 ft AGL the fog hides everything. What now, and what is the hazard?
questions.a: Go missed immediately [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(e)(1)]]. From below the MDA past the MAP, the published missed does not necessarily give obstacle clearance or separation [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]]. Get an amended clearance from ATC as soon as possible; if you can't, rejoin a published segment of the missed and its altitudes [[33:452|AIM 5-4-21h]].

questions.q: You push the power up in the dark with full flaps. What is the order, and what traps wait?
questions.a: Power, attitude, configuration. Hold the nose down against the pitch-up, raise flaps in steps as you accelerate, and don't climb out of ground effect too soon [[24:182|AFH 9-11]] [[24:183|AFH 9-12]]. Forgetting the flaps makes a high-drag go-around that drains energy near the ground [[24:103|AFH 4-17]].

questions.q: You press the go-around controls, but the mode annunciator shows the autopilot in a wings-level mode, not on the missed course. What do you do?
questions.a: Fly the airplane first. Reduce the level of automation or hand-fly, then anticipate, act and verify as you set it up again [[30:51|RMH 7-2]]. A change in navigation source can drop the autopilot to wings level [[30:52|RMH 7-3]].

questions.q: Tower says: "Fly heading 360, climb and maintain 3,000." The published missed is straight ahead to 1,800, then a right turn. What do you fly and say?
questions.a: Fly the tower's heading and altitude; ATC vectors replace the published missed [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21d]]. Read it back, and advise ATC that you are on the missed and why [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]].

questions.q: The weather is now below minimums and not expected to improve for two hours. Hold, try again, or divert?
questions.a: Divert now and request clearance to the alternate [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]]. Your IFR fuel plan assumed the alternate plus 45 minutes [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]]. With 1:40 aboard and 30 minutes to go, you land with about 1:10, but two hours of holding is impossible.

skills.do: Start the missed approach promptly at the MAP or DA, or when told, and report it to ATC with the reason.
skills.practice: On every practice approach, say "going missed" at the MAP, then make the call: "missed approach, (reason), request ___" [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[29:105|IPH 2-45]].

skills.do: Apply go-around power and set the pitch attitude for the climb.
skills.practice: Full power smoothly, carb heat off, hold the climb attitude against the pitch-up with forward pressure and right rudder, then rough trim [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

skills.do: Configure the airplane per the POH, get a positive rate of climb, and accelerate to the appropriate airspeed ±10 knots (ACS IR.VI.C.S3).
skills.practice: Raise flaps in small steps as the airplane accelerates; gear up after a positive rate of climb, if retractable [[24:182|AFH 9-11]] [[24:183|AFH 9-12]].

skills.do: Use the recommended checklist items for the missed approach or go-around.
skills.practice: Learn a flow (power, attitude, flaps, rate, gear, navigate, talk) and confirm it with the POH checklist once stable. Airplane control comes first [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

skills.do: Fly the published missed approach or the alternate missed ATC assigns.
skills.practice: Brief the missed text out loud before every approach [[29:182|IPH 4-42]]. Practice early missed approaches: fly to the MAP at or above the MDA, then turn [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

skills.do: Tell ATC or the evaluator if you can't comply with a clearance, restriction or climb gradient.
skills.practice: Before each approach, convert the required gradient to a climb rate at your expected groundspeed [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. Practice saying "unable" and offering an alternative, such as declining an alternate missed that needs equipment you don't have [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]].

skills.do: Hold the recommended airspeed ±10 knots; heading, course or bearing ±10°; and altitudes ±100 ft (ACS IR.VI.C.S7).
skills.practice: Rough trim as soon as the climb is set, then trim precisely when stable [[24:182|AFH 9-11]]. Keep a full scan through the turn and the level-off at the missed approach altitude.

skills.do: Use the MFD or other moving map to monitor position and track on the missed.
skills.practice: During the turn, check the moving map against the CDI [[23:29|IFH 1-10]] and confirm the GPS has sequenced to the missed approach leg [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].

skills.do: Use SRM, or CRM with a crew, during the missed approach.
skills.practice: Set the missed approach altitude in the preselector early [[29:177|IPH 4-37]], use automation to cut workload, and anticipate, act, verify each mode change [[30:51|RMH 7-2]] [[30:56|RMH 8-3]].

skills.do: Request another approach, the alternate, a holding fix or another clearance limit, as appropriate or as the evaluator directs.
skills.practice: Decide before the approach what you will ask for after a miss, then request it right after the missed approach call [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21f]].

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a 14 CFR 91.175(c)(3) visual reference for descending below the MDA?
options: The visual glideslope indicator
The touchdown zone markings
The runway end identifier lights
The airport rotating beacon
quiz.why: The rotating beacon is not on the list. The visual glideslope indicator, REIL and touchdown zone markings are [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)]].

quiz.q: On an ILS, where is the missed approach point?
options: At the runway threshold
Over the middle marker
At the DA/DH on the glideslope
When the timer from the FAF runs out
quiz.why: For a precision approach, the MAP is where you reach the DA or DH on the glideslope [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

quiz.q: Unless the chart says otherwise, missed approach obstacle protection assumes a climb of at least:
options: 200 ft/NM
300 ft/NM
152 ft/NM
400 ft/NM
quiz.why: 200 ft/NM is standard. 400 ft/NM applies only to Copter approaches [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

quiz.q: You start a missed approach 2 NM before the MAP. The missed begins with a climbing right turn. Unless ATC says otherwise, you:
options: Turn right right away to save time, since the climb is already under way
Fly the approach course to the MAP at or above the MDA, then turn
Climb straight ahead past the MAP until at the missed altitude
Hold the MDA and keep flying the approach until ATC gives you instructions
quiz.why: No allowance is made for an early turn, so fly the approach to the MAP at or above the MDA or DA/DH before turning [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

quiz.q: Circling to land, you lose sight of the runway. What is your first turn?
options: Toward the missed approach fix, whichever way is shorter
A climbing turn toward the landing runway
Away from the airport to stay clear of traffic
Wings level, straight ahead to the missed altitude
quiz.why: Make an initial climbing turn toward the landing runway and continue until established on the missed approach course [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21c]].

quiz.q: After you begin the approach, ATC issues an alternate missed approach that needs DME, which the published approach doesn't. You may:
options: Not refuse it, because it is an ATC instruction
Accept it only after reading the NOTAM
Accept it only if the weather is above minimums
Reject it
quiz.why: Issued after you begin the approach, you may reject an alternate missed that needs equipment not required for the published approach [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]].

quiz.q: On a non-WAAS GPS you activate the missed approach 1 NM before the MAWP. What happens?
options: The receiver sequences ahead and turns you toward the missed approach fix at once
The approach mode cancels, the CDI goes to ±5 NM, and the receiver stops guiding
Nothing changes in the receiver until you cross the runway threshold itself
The CDI goes to ±1 NM and the receiver keeps navigating to the MAWP
quiz.why: Early activation changes the CDI to ±1 NM, but the receiver still navigates to the MAWP and won't sequence past it. Don't turn before the MAWP [[33:97|AIM 1-1-17b5(f)]].

quiz.q: The moment you decide to go around, what is your first concern?
options: Flap retraction
Power
Gear retraction
Calling ATC
quiz.why: Power is the pilot's first concern, then attitude, then configuration [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

quiz.q: You reach the missed approach holding fix at 5,000 ft MSL. What is the maximum holding airspeed?
options: 200 KIAS
230 KIAS
210 KIAS
265 KIAS
quiz.why: From the MHA to 6,000 ft MSL the maximum is 200 KIAS. 230 is for 6,001 to 14,000 ft [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].

takeaways: At the DA or MAP without the 91.175(c) requirements, go missed immediately. No waiting, no peeking lower.
Know how this approach defines its MAP: DA, NAVAID, fix, waypoint or the clock from the FAF.
Protection assumes the missed starts at the MAP, at or above the MDA or DA, climbing at least 200 ft/NM. Do the fpm math before the approach.
Early missed: fly the approach to the MAP, then turn. Circling missed: climbing turn toward the runway.
Power, attitude, configuration. Then navigate, then tell ATC and ask for what you want next.
ATC vectors and alternate missed approaches replace the published missed. Say "unable" if you can't comply.
Anticipate, act, verify with the GPS and autopilot, and hand-fly when they surprise you.
cfi_notes: IPH 4-41 says obstacle clearance "is not provided" by the published missed when it starts other than at the MAP, below the MDA or DA, or while circling [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]. The current AIM says "not necessarily provided" [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]]. Teach the AIM wording.

The IFH uses "MAP" for both the missed approach point and the missed approach procedure ("When a MAP is initiated...") [[23:312|IFH 10-21]]. Students get confused; make them say "point" or "procedure."
IFH 10-21 lists "VASI" among the visual references [[23:312|IFH 10-21]]. The current rule says "visual glideslope indicator" [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)(vi)]]. Use the regulation's wording.

The IPH chart examples (Orlando, Burbank, Daggett) date from 2010 and 2011 and are marked not for navigation. The IPH also says climb notes give fpm examples with gradients coming later [[29:181|IPH 4-41]]; the current AIM uses ft/NM with the TPP conversion table [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. Have students work the same problems on current charts.
AFH Figure 9-12 shows a twin with retractable gear. Teach the order (power, attitude, configuration) and take the flap speeds and steps from the student's own POH.

Examiners commonly probe: what an approach clearance includes, early missed approaches (fly to the MAP), the circling missed turn, alternate missed approaches, climb gradient math, and GPS sequencing. Have the student brief the missed out loud before every approach.

IFH 1-23 says to use the "next higher" category's minimums when maneuvering faster than your category [[23:42|IFH 1-23]]. The IPH says to use the category that fits the speed, which can be two categories up (Category B at 145 knots uses D) [[29:148|IPH 4-8]]. Teach the IPH version.
Common student errors: turning the moment they decide to go missed, forgetting to activate the GPS missed, leaving the MDA in the preselector, and flying the whole missed without telling ATC.
gaps: Go-around power, pitch attitude, flap retraction speeds, Vx/Vy and the missed approach checklist for the training airplane come from its POH/AFM, which is not in these sources.
Specific GPS navigator, FMS and autopilot go-around (GA button) operation depends on each avionics manual; the sources describe only general behavior.
The TPP climb rate table (page D1) and current approach charts are not in the sources; the chart examples are older IPH charts.
Multiengine and engine-out missed approach content is left out (single-engine land only).
For S9, the callout and intervention guidance in the sources (AC 120-71B, IPH crew briefing) is for multi-crew operators; no FAA source gives a single-pilot GA callout script.

activities.title: True or false: when to go missed
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: If the reported visibility is at minimums, you may land even if you judge flight visibility to be lower.
cards.why: No. Only the pilot can judge flight visibility. If it is below the chart minimum, go missed regardless of the report [[23:313|IFH 10-22]].

cards.s: Seeing only the approach lights at the DA, you may descend to 100 ft above the touchdown zone elevation.
cards.why: Yes. Lower than that needs the red terminating bars or red side row bars too [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)(i)]].

cards.s: While circling, losing sight of the airport only because of a normal bank does not by itself require a missed approach.
You may continue below the DA with the runway in sight even if you can't reach it with a normal rate of descent.
cards.why: No. You must also be continuously in a position to land at a normal rate of descent using normal maneuvers [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(1)]].

cards.s: After descending below the MDA, you must go missed if the runway environment is no longer visible.
cards.why: Yes, unless the loss of sight is only from normal banking while circling [[29:180|IPH 4-40]].

cards.s: On an LPV approach you should wait for the GPS distance to reach zero before going missed.
cards.why: No. You go missed at the DA without the required references; don't wait for the distance to reach zero [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d7]].

activities.title: Where is the MAP?
activities.intro: Tap an approach, then how you find its missed approach point.

pairs.r: Reaching the DA on the glideslope or glidepath

pairs.l: VOR approach, VOR on the field
NDB away from the field, no fix
pairs.r: Time from the FAF at your groundspeed
The localizer course and the charted DME
The missed approach waypoint, flown over

activities.title: Missed approach numbers
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: The missed approach needs the standard 200 ft/NM. Your groundspeed on the climb is 90 knots. What climb rate do you need?
items.why: 90 knots ÷ 60 = 1.5 NM a minute. 1.5 × 200 = 300 fpm. The TPP rate of climb table does the same conversion [[29:34|IPH Figure 1-17]] [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

items.q: Burbank's ILS RWY 8 missed needs 334 ft/NM. Your groundspeed is 120 knots. What climb rate do you need?
Daggett's missed needs 220 ft/NM to 8,000. Your groundspeed is 90 knots. What climb rate do you need?
A timed approach has 5.5 NM from the FAF to the MAP. Your groundspeed on final is 110 knots. How many seconds after the FAF do you reach the MAP?
items.why: 5.5 ÷ 110 = 0.05 hr = 3.0 minutes = 180 seconds. Start the clock at the FAF [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

items.q: After a missed you have 1 hour 40 minutes of fuel. The alternate is 30 minutes away and you want to land there with the 45 minutes your IFR fuel plan assumed. How many minutes can you hold first?
items.why: 100 - 30 - 45 = 25 minutes. The IFR fuel plan covers the alternate plus 45 minutes at normal cruise [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]].

activities.title: Find it on the Orlando chart
activities.intro: Drag each name to its numbered pin.

pins.label: Maximum altitude for an early missed

activities.title: Protected or not?
activities.intro: Tap a clue, then tap where it belongs.

items.t: Start the missed at the DA on the glideslope
Start at the MAP, at or above the MDA
Go missed early, fly to the MAP at the MDA, then turn
Turn toward the missed fix before reaching the MAP
Go around from 200 ft below the MDA, past the MAP
Climb only 150 ft/NM where 200 ft/NM is assumed
Leave the missed for a shortcut before reaching a safe altitude

activities.title: Fly the missed approach
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Apply full power smoothly, carb heat off
Set the climb pitch attitude and rough trim
Raise the flaps in steps as you accelerate
Positive rate of climb: gear up, if retractable
Fly the missed approach course, turning only at or after the MAP
Tell ATC "missed approach" and request your next clearance

activities.title: LPV to minimums, then the missed
activities.intro: You are flying N123AB, single pilot, on an RNAV (GPS) RWY 26 approach to LPV minimums at Daggett. The missed approach needs 220 ft/NM to 8,000, then you hold at NULMN. Your alternate has good weather and you have plenty of fuel.

steps.s: You reach the DA on the glidepath. Nothing is in sight. The GPS shows 0.7 NM to the threshold.
options: Level off and fly until the distance reads 0.0
Go missed now
Descend 100 ft more and look again
Switch to LNAV minimums and continue
steps.why: On LPV you go missed at the DA without the required references; don't wait for the distance to reach zero [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d7]] [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(e)(1)]].

steps.s: You say "going missed." What do you do first?
options: Raise all the flaps
Call approach control
Full power and set the climb pitch attitude
Press autopilot buttons and watch what happens
steps.why: Power first, then attitude, then configuration. Raising all the flaps at once can make the airplane settle [[24:182|AFH 9-11]].

steps.s: Flaps are coming up in steps. Groundspeed is 100 knots and the VSI shows 300 fpm.
options: That's fine, any climb is enough
Turn toward AMAKE early to shorten the climb
Level off until the missed approach fix
You need about 370 fpm: pitch for best climb and tell ATC if you can't make it
steps.why: 100 ÷ 60 × 220 = about 367 fpm [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. No allowance is made for an early turn [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]], and you must advise ATC if unable (ACS IR.VI.C.S6).

steps.s: Climbing on the missed, approach control asks your intentions. The weather is now below minimums.
options: "Missed approach, request the same approach again right away to see if it clears"
"Missed approach, weather below minimums, request clearance to my alternate"
Say nothing about the weather until you are level at 8,000 and established in the hold
Squawk 7700 and tell ATC you are declaring an emergency for the weather
steps.why: Advise ATC of the missed and the reason, then request a specific action such as your alternate [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]].

steps.s: ATC: "Hold at NULMN as published, expect further clearance in 15 minutes." You reach NULMN at 7,000, still climbing.
options: Enter the hold, keep climbing to 8,000 in it, and report time and altitude at the fix
Ask for a shortcut toward the alternate before reaching 8,000, since the hold is only a delay
Stop the climb at 7,000 to save fuel and fly the hold at that altitude until further clearance
Leave the hold for the alternate as soon as you reach it, since the missed has taken you to the fix
steps.why: The missed says to continue the climb in the hold to 8,000 [[29:187|IPH Figure 4-26]]. Report time and altitude at the holding fix [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]], and don't leave the missed before a safe altitude [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21g]].

final_quiz.q: The missed approach requires 300 ft/NM. You expect 110 knots groundspeed on the climb. What climb rate do you need?
options: 330 fpm
500 fpm
600 fpm
550 fpm
final_quiz.why: 110 knots ÷ 60 = 1.83 NM a minute; × 300 ft = 550 fpm [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]]. 500 fpm would work only at 100 knots.

final_quiz.q: A timed approach has 5.5 NM from the FAF to the MAP. Your groundspeed on final is 100 knots. About how long after the FAF is the MAP?
final_quiz.why: 5.5 ÷ 100 × 60 = 3.3 minutes, about 3:18. 3:40 is the 90-knot time and 2:45 the 120-knot time in the Orlando table [[29:184|IPH Figure 4-23]] [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

final_quiz.q: After the MAP you see the runway lights and descend below the MDA. At 300 ft AGL fog hides the runway. What now?
options: Go missed now, knowing the published missed may not clear obstacles from here, and ask ATC for an amended clearance
Level off at this altitude and wait a short time for the approach lights to reappear, then continue the descent if they do
Descend to 100 ft above the TDZE on instruments alone, and then look again for the runway environment to reappear
Climb back up to the MDA, level off there, and keep looking for the runway before you decide to go missed
final_quiz.why: Once below the MDA, go missed if the runway environment is no longer visible [[29:180|IPH 4-40]]. From there obstacle clearance is not necessarily provided [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21h]], so contact ATC for an amended clearance [[33:452|AIM 5-4-21h]].

final_quiz.q: Reported visibility is 1 SM and the chart minimum is 1 SM. At the MDA you see the runway lights, but flight visibility looks like 1/2 SM. What do you do?
options: Land, because the reported visibility meets the chart minimum
Continue down to 100 ft above the TDZE and make the decision to land there
Go missed, because flight visibility is below the minimum
Ask the tower for RVR and land if it reads 5,000 feet or better
final_quiz.why: Only the pilot can judge flight visibility. If it is less than the approach requires, go missed regardless of the reported visibility [[23:313|IFH 10-22]] [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(2)]].

final_quiz.q: On an ILS at the DA you see the approach lights, but not the red terminating bars or red side row bars. Using only those lights, how low may you descend?
options: To 100 ft above the touchdown zone elevation
To touchdown
Not below the DA
To 200 ft above the airport elevation
final_quiz.why: Approach lights alone take you to 100 ft above the TDZE. Below that you need the red bars or another listed reference [[60:472|14 CFR 91.175(c)(3)(i)]].

final_quiz.q: The missed approach requires 350 ft/NM. You will climb out with a 20-knot tailwind. How does the tailwind affect the climb?
options: It raises the climb rate in fpm that you need
It has no effect, because the gradient is fixed
It only matters above 1,000 ft AGL
It lowers the climb rate you need
final_quiz.why: A higher groundspeed than expected increases the climb rate (fpm) needed to meet the same gradient [[33:450|AIM 5-4-21b]].

final_quiz.q: Flying an LPV, you reach the DA with nothing in sight. The GPS shows 0.6 NM to the threshold. What do you do?
options: Switch to LNAV minimums and continue
Level off and fly until the distance reads 0.0
Descend 100 ft more and look again
Go missed now
final_quiz.why: On LPV and LNAV/VNAV the missed starts at the DA without the required references. Don't wait for the distance to reach zero [[33:106|AIM 1-1-18d7]].

final_quiz.q: On the Orlando ILS RWY 7 you decide to go missed early, before BUVAY, at 2,000 ft. The missed is a climb to 1,200 maximum to SOTCO. What is correct?
options: Climb to 2,500 now and turn toward OVIDO, since an early missed lets you skip the course
Hold 2,000 level until you reach the MAP, then start the climb to the missed altitude
Climb to 1,500 now and fly direct OVIDO, because the 1,200 maximum only applies after the MAP
Continue the descent to 1,200 and fly the course to the MAP, then follow the missed
final_quiz.why: With a maximum altitude between the FAF and MAP, comply with it, even if that means continuing the descent [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]]. At Orlando you may need to descend to 1,200 before the MAP [[29:181|IPH 4-41]].

final_quiz.q: Before you begin the approach, ATC issues an alternate missed approach that needs a receiver you don't have. What are your options?
options: You must accept it, because an alternate missed issued before the approach is a mandatory ATC instruction
Accept the whole procedure, request a different approach, or coordinate other action such as your alternate
Accept it for now, then quietly fly the published missed instead once you reach the missed approach point
Reject only the alternate missed and fly the rest of the approach as cleared by ATC, using the published missed
final_quiz.why: Issued before the approach, you either accept the entire procedure, request a different approach, or coordinate other action [[33:451|AIM 5-4-21e]]. Rejecting just the alternate missed applies only after you begin the approach.

final_quiz.q: You reach a standard holding fix on the missed from the parallel entry sector. What do you do after crossing the fix?
options: Parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding side for 1 minute, then turn more than 180° toward the holding side
Turn outbound to a heading 30° off the holding course, on the holding side, for 1 minute, then turn to intercept the inbound course
Turn right at once and fly the pattern straight away, timing the outbound leg for 1 minute from the abeam position
Fly outbound on the reciprocal of the inbound course for 2 minutes, then turn left to rejoin the fix
final_quiz.why: That is the parallel entry. Turning right at once is the direct entry; the 30° heading is the teardrop [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]].

final_quiz.q: You leveled at the MDA on the autopilot and never reset the altitude preselector. What problem shows up when you go missed?
options: The autopilot disconnects as soon as the missed approach is activated
The GPS refuses to sequence past the MAWP until you reset the altitude window
Flight director guidance for the missed isn't accurate
The CDI scale changes to ±5 NM for the whole missed approach segment
final_quiz.why: Accurate flight director guidance is not available on the missed if the MDA is left in the window. Set the missed approach altitude once level at the MDA [[29:177|IPH 4-37]].

final_quiz.q: After a missed, the weather is below minimums and won't improve for two hours. You have 1:20 of fuel, and the alternate is 25 minutes away. Best request?
options: Hold for improvement
Clearance to the alternate now
Another approach right away
A contact approach
final_quiz.why: Request clearance to the alternate [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]]. You land with about 55 minutes; two hours of holding is impossible, and the IFR fuel plan assumed alternate plus 45 minutes [[60:469|14 CFR 91.167(a)(3)]].

final_quiz.q: You go missed because you never saw the runway. Which call to approach control best follows the AIM?
options: "Request vectors to the approach again" and no reason for the missed
"Going around" and nothing more until you level off at the missed altitude
"Missed approach, runway not in sight, request the ILS again"
"Climbing to 3,000" only, with no mention of the missed approach or the reason
final_quiz.why: Advise ATC of the missed approach and the reason, then request a specific action such as another approach [[34:4|AIM 5-5-5a]] [[34:5|AIM 5-5-5a]].
